rubric.item: Uses independent write and read clocks with different, unrelated frequencies
rubric.evidence: C14 sweeps clock pairs 1:1, 2:3, 3:2, 10:1, 1:10 with randomized phase; F12 asynchronous clock relationships

rubric.item: Checks end to end that no data is lost, duplicated or reordered across the clock crossing
rubric.evidence: C9: scoreboard queue push on accepted write, pop and compare on accepted read; drained count equals accepted writes

rubric.item: Checks full asserts after exactly 2^ADDR_WIDTH writes with no reads
rubric.evidence: C3: Write DEPTH words with wr_en held and no reads → all accepted; full=1 right after the DEPTH-th accepted write; DEPTH=2^ADDR_WIDTH

rubric.item: Notes that full and empty may assert late (pessimistically) because of synchronizer latency, and checks they are never optimistic
rubric.evidence: F9 'flags are conservative'; F14 'never optimistic'; C7 no optimistic flag

rubric.item: Checks that the pointers crossing domains are Gray coded, with one bit changing per increment
rubric.evidence: C8: $onehot(wr_ptr_gray ^ $past(wr_ptr_gray)) on each fire; F8 Gray pointer encoding

rubric.item: Covers resetting the write and read domains independently or at different times
rubric.evidence: C15: (a) wr_rst_n only while rd active, (b) rd_rst_n only while wr active, (c) both; coverage reset event wr-only, rd-only, both

rubric.item: Covers pointer wrap-around
rubric.evidence: C10: pointers wrap several times; coverage 'pointer wrap' bins; Edge case 5

rubric.item: Checks that the first arbitration after reset grants requester 0 when several requesters are active
rubric.evidence: C2: After reset, drive req=all-ones only; first grant is index 0 (not N-1).

rubric.item: Checks round-robin order under continuous contention, with each requester served in turn
rubric.evidence: C5: grant sequence is 0,1,…,N-1,0,… with no skips or repeats.

rubric.item: Checks the grant doesn't change while a burst is in progress even if req changes (no preemption)
rubric.evidence: C8: toggle req of all other indices for 1000 cycles → grant unchanged.

rubric.item: Checks the grant is released after burst_done and a new arbitration only starts afterwards
rubric.evidence: C10/C11: burst_done at edge T → grant==0; grant appears after edge T+1 (not T).

rubric.item: Checks grant is always zero or one-hot and grant_valid equals the OR of grant
rubric.evidence: C3: grant is one-hot or zero at every cycle; C13: grant_valid == (|grant).

rubric.item: Covers a single requester being granted repeatedly when nobody else requests
rubric.evidence: C6: requester k granted again when req high only for k; edge case 11 back-to-back same requester.

rubric.item: Includes burst_done arriving on the first cycle of a grant (one-cycle burst) as an edge case
Covers the round-robin pointer wrapping from the last index back to index 0
rubric.evidence: C7: wrap to 0 after serving 3; cp_last_idx notes wrap N-1→0; edge case 2.

rubric.item: Checks data and the last flag come out in the order they were written
rubric.evidence: C5 drains in write order; C12 'rd_last equals the wr_last written for that entry, in order'; C8 scoreboard order

rubric.item: Checks full asserts after exactly DEPTH writes and that writes are refused while full
rubric.evidence: C3: 'Exactly DEPTH writes accepted; full=1 after the DEPTH-th; wr_ready=0 thereafter'; C4 blocks writes at full

rubric.item: Checks rd_valid stays low and nothing is read while the FIFO is empty
rubric.evidence: C7: 'With rd_ready=1 and empty=1... rd_ptr does not move; count stays 0; rd_valid=0'

rubric.item: Checks fill_level tracks occupancy, including during simultaneous read and write
rubric.evidence: C8 count unchanged with both fires; C1/C3 fill_level checks; F5 fill_level derived from count; C14 fill_level width

rubric.item: Covers simultaneous read and write both when the FIFO is full and when it is empty
rubric.evidence: C9 at full wr_valid and rd_ready together; C10 empty with wr_valid and rd_ready together

rubric.item: Covers read and write pointer wrap-around
rubric.evidence: C11 'Pointer wrap observed'; cp_ptr_wrap coverpoint; edge case 4

rubric.item: Checks behaviour when reset is asserted while the FIFO holds data
rubric.evidence: C2 'Reset mid-operation with entries stored'; C15 reset while full; C1

rubric.item: Covers read-side back-pressure (rd_ready low while data is available)
rubric.evidence: C6 rd_ready=0 with rd_valid=1 data stable; cp_stall_len; edge case 8
